53-3011.00.title: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
53-3011.00.description: Drive ambulance or assist ambulance driver in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons. Assist in lifting patients.

tasks.text: Remove and replace soiled linens or equipment to maintain sanitary conditions.
Drive ambulances or assist ambulance drivers in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons.
Report facts concerning accidents or emergencies to hospital personnel or law enforcement officials.
Place patients on stretchers, and load stretchers into ambulances, usually with assistance from other attendants.
Accompany and assist emergency medical technicians on calls.
Replace supplies and disposable items on ambulances.
Perform minor maintenance on emergency medical services vehicles, such as ambulances.
Clean and wash rigs, ambulances, or equipment.
Administer first aid, such as bandaging, splinting, or administering oxygen.

dwas: Maintain vehicles in good working condition.
Provide first aid or rescue assistance in emergencies.
Stock medical or patient care supplies.
Notify others of emergencies, problems, or hazards.
Hold patients to ensure proper positioning or safety.

jobZone.name: Job Zone 1-2: Very Little to Some Preparation Needed
jobZone.experience: Some occupations may need little or no previous experience; others require several months to a year of experience. For example, landscaping and groundskeeping workers might require very little training or previous experience, while agricultural equipment operators can benefit from on-the job training.
jobZone.education: Usually requires a high school diploma or GED, though some occupations may not.
jobZone.training: Ranges from a few days to one year of on-the-job training.
jobZone.examples: These occupations involve following instructions and often involve using your knowledge and skills to help others. Examples include dishwashers, landscaping and groundskeeping workers, counter and rental clerks, dental laboratory technicians, and security guards.
